A first-class MiMo provider profile SHALL select MiMo for configured Xiaomi or MiMo models, preserve provider-internal reasoning only inside bounded provider request state, apply agentic sampling, normalize native and MiMo textual calls from content or reasoning, buffer tool-bearing streams until safe normalization, emit no raw provider reasoning to any client, prevent internal compatibility or revision fallback instructions and outputs from entering transcript history or the user stream, and retain schema and policy validation before execution.
2. BEFORE the first tool-bearing task on a provider profile, Ion SHALL run a harmless multi-turn tool-call canary, record a secret-free capability mode, and select native-buffered, textual-buffered, compatibility, or an available fallback without mutating the user workspace.
3. WORKSPACE tools SHALL safely create missing file parents, accept absolute paths only when contained by the registered root, translate leading change-directory intent into a bounded working directory, and return structured corrective results for unavailable executables without weakening traversal or symlink isolation.
4. AN accepted outcome SHALL persist criterion-linked dependency work items with one authoritative pending, ready, running, verifying, blocked, or completed state; verified artifacts SHALL advance covered items and unlock only dependency-ready work across turn and daemon replacement.
5. A recovery retry SHALL change a material execution strategy such as parser, buffering, prompt mode, context, tool surface, credential, or provider; prediction mismatch state SHALL be keyed to the exact normalized action and scoped to the current turn; and the runtime SHALL detect exhausted strategies instead of repeating an identical request as recovery or allowing unrelated prior actions to force revision.
6. A bounded no-activity watchdog SHALL emit truthful recovery state, cancel the stalled attempt, and start a fresh continuation from the durable checkpoint; browser and TUI reducers SHALL distinguish running, recovering, incomplete, failed, interrupted, and completed states without phantom work.
7. AN ordinary model final SHALL NOT end a turn when it exposes internal control flow, refers to an undelivered earlier answer, omits the subject of the original request, or ends research without substantive cited evidence or an explicit evidence limitation; an active outcome contract additionally SHALL require server-verified criterion coverage and evidence-bound completion, or a real authority, safety, decision, cancellation, or exhausted-budget boundary.
8. A production-path fault suite SHALL prove MiMo native and textual calls, multi-turn preflight, malformed-call strategy change, exact-action turn-scoped mismatch isolation, typed revision continuation with no transcript poisoning, zero raw-reasoning client events, rejection and repair of a MatrixMCL-style false final, nested and wrong-form path recovery, encrypted work-item restart, watchdog continuation, truthful terminal UI restoration, and refusal of premature completion.

## Requirement 53: Canonical tool-lifecycle events for the Ion Computer

**User Story:** As a user watching Ion work, I want every real tool interaction to drive a durable visual event, so that the computer shows what the agent is actually doing instead of inventing a theatrical activity stream.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. EVERY model-visible operation executed through the shared production tool manager SHALL emit a canonical lifecycle of requested, awaiting_approval when applicable, started, bounded progress when available, and exactly one completed, failed, denied, interrupted, or outcome_unknown terminal event; the tool call SHALL trigger the activity and the real tool response SHALL be the content source.
2. EACH ComputerEvent SHALL carry a protocol version, event ID, durable sequence, actor, session, turn, task or outcome, agent, tool-call, tool and operation identifiers, scope, risk class, phase, timestamp, display-kind hint, bounded source references, and terminal status without exposing private reasoning or secret values.
3. COMPUTER events SHALL reference the authoritative ToolEvent, approval, artifact, process, browser, project, or evidence record and SHALL NOT create a second execution or completion truth.
4. STREAMING tools MAY emit coalesced progress and content deltas subject to per-tool size, rate, retention, and backpressure bounds; slow or disconnected clients SHALL NOT block execution or force unbounded server or browser memory.
5. RECONNECT, client refresh, route change, daemon restart, duplicate delivery, retention gaps, and out-of-order parallel completion SHALL reconstruct one deterministic scoped activity history and current computer state using replay or an explicit snapshot-plus-gap boundary.
6. A production-path test SHALL prove lifecycle correlation for success, approval, denial, streaming, failure, interruption, uncertain outcome, duplicate replay, restart, and concurrent agents without phantom activity or false completion.

## Requirement 54: Validated semantic display models derived from tool responses

**User Story:** As a user, I want Ion to turn raw tool responses into clear native views, so that I can understand the agent's working state without reading protocol payloads, terminal noise, screenshots, or copied website chrome.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A versioned adapter registry SHALL map supported tool calls and responses into generated, runtime-validated display models; structured response fields SHALL be preferred over model-authored extraction and unsupported tools SHALL fall back to an honest generic action and result view.
2. ADAPTERS SHALL be deterministic for URLs, queries, repository paths, files, code ranges, commands, exit state, process state, tables, document structure, artifacts, citations, and other structured fields; model-produced summaries MAY supplement but SHALL NOT replace or contradict source data.
3. EVERY displayed datum SHALL be classified as observed, generated, summarized, inferred, or unavailable and SHALL retain a bounded reference to the corresponding source event, result, artifact, URL, revision, or command output.
4. DISPLAY models SHALL use a small reusable vocabulary for search results, reader content, navigation trees, code, terminal output, diffs, processes, tables, charts, documents, artifacts, tasks, agents, approvals, errors, and empty or degraded states rather than reproducing each external product pixel-for-pixel.
5. RAW tool payloads, arbitrary HTML, scripts, styles, terminal control sequences, data URLs, and unvalidated media SHALL NOT enter the application DOM; text, links, media, code, and structured values SHALL pass schema validation, normalization, sanitization, redaction, and explicit size limits first.
6. ADAPTER and display-schema evolution SHALL preserve replay of retained events through versioned migration or an explicit unsupported-version view and SHALL never silently reinterpret historical evidence.
7. A contract suite SHALL prove exact extraction, truth classification, evidence linkage, fallback behavior, malformed and oversized result handling, schema migration, and stable rendering for every registered display model.

## Requirement 55: Live, inspectable, and replayable Ion Computer experience

**User Story:** As a user, I want to watch my agent work inside a calm Ion-native computer, so that substantial delegated work feels visible and understandable without becoming a fake remote desktop.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE web experience SHALL provide a resizable split between persistent conversation or task activity and a Ion Computer stage, with an accessible full-screen mode and adaptive behavior from 390px mobile through wide desktop.
2. THE computer header SHALL continuously show the bound task or outcome, current agent, active Ion application, plain-language action, running, awaiting decision, recovering, blocked, failed, interrupted, or completed state, and the latest durable event time.
3. FOLLOW LIVE SHALL be the default; users SHALL be able to pause following, inspect an earlier event or artifact, scrub or navigate the durable timeline, and use Back to live without changing the agent's execution state or losing their inspection position.
4. WATCH state and USER EXPLORE state SHALL remain distinct. Inspecting a result SHALL be read-only, while steering, retrying, taking over, approving, denying, pausing, resuming, cancelling, or requesting another action SHALL use explicit production commands and existing policy boundaries.
5. MOTION SHALL only communicate a real state transition. Ion SHALL NOT fabricate cursor movement, clicks, typing, tool usage, progress, or completion; reduced-motion mode SHALL preserve all information without animation.
6. THE experience SHALL meet WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard and screen-reader critical paths, localization-safe layout, bounded virtualization for long histories, dark and light themes, and comprehensible loading, empty, degraded, gap, and failure states.
7. THE TUI SHALL expose the same ordered action, status, truth class, source, approval, artifact, and replay semantics in a terminal-appropriate form without pretending to reproduce the graphical computer.
8. Real-client tests SHALL prove resizing, full screen, Follow live, historical inspection, Back to live, explicit steering, reconnect, refresh, route changes, mobile, keyboard, screen reader, reduced motion, and long-event virtualization.

## Requirement 56: Ion-native application renderers for agent work

**User Story:** As a user, I want the computer to select an understandable application for each kind of work, so that web research, code, commands, data, and deliverables share one coherent Ion visual language.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A Research Browser SHALL render search query and results, opened URL, title, source, extracted navigation, headings, readable content, links, citations, media references, and browse state from real search and browser responses without depending on third-party iframe permission.
2. A Repository and Code application SHALL render provider or workspace identity, revision, branch, path tree, selected file, language, bounded code ranges, matches, commits, diffs, and diagnostics from repository, browser, project, Git, and file-tool results.
3. A Terminal and Process application SHALL render working directory, redacted command, bounded streaming output, exit status, duration, process and service state, retries, cancellation, and related artifacts while neutralizing control sequences and secret material.
4. Document, Artifact, and Data applications SHALL render generated or inspected documents, tables, charts, reports, images, presentations, and downloadable artifacts from validated structures with provenance, version, completion, and verification state.
5. A Task and Agent application SHALL render the authoritative outcome, work items, current and historical agent assignments, bounded parallel activity, blockers, decisions, evidence, produced artifacts, and completion coverage without exposing private chain of thought.
6. SEMANTIC rendering SHALL be the default. A sanitized screenshot or visual snapshot MAY be shown on demand when appearance is itself relevant or semantic extraction is insufficient, and SHALL be labeled as captured evidence rather than used as the primary second-by-second transport.
7. RENDERERS SHALL register by generated display-kind contract, share the Ion design system and generic primitives, and degrade to the generic evidence view when a specialized application is absent or incompatible.
8. A renderer matrix SHALL prove real search, article, GitHub or GitLab repository, local workspace, code, terminal, process, diff, document, tabular data, artifact, error, screenshot fallback, and unsupported-tool journeys.
9. Public-web research that does not require direct page interaction SHALL start with Tavily structured search when configured, automatically fall back to the configured SearXNG JSON service when Tavily is unavailable or empty, return bounded ranked source metadata and a source-backed overview to the Ion-native Research application, and reserve semantic fetch, native Chromium/CDP, or graphical computer interaction for selected source text, authentication, JavaScript-only interaction, navigation, downloads, visual inspection, or work earlier layers cannot complete.

## Requirement 57: Parallel-agent workspaces and causally explicit human interaction

**User Story:** As a user supervising substantial work, I want to see what each active agent is doing and interact without racing execution, so that parallelism remains understandable and under my control.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. EACH parent and sub-agent SHALL have a stable scoped workspace identity, assignment, current application and action, status, recent evidence, budget state, and produced artifacts derived from authoritative task and tool events.
2. THE computer SHALL provide an aggregate workspace plus selection of one agent at a time, visibly distinguish foreground inspection from background execution, and preserve independent Follow live positions when switching agents.
3. PARALLEL events SHALL remain causally ordered per agent and correlated to parent work items; aggregate presentation SHALL NOT imply an order that conflicts with durable timestamps, sequence boundaries, dependencies, or completion evidence.
4. USER steering SHALL target an explicit task, agent, tool action, or artifact revision, reconcile against current execution state, and reject stale, contradictory, cross-scope, or unauthorized commands rather than applying them to whichever window is visible.
5. TAKEOVER of a terminal or browser SHALL acquire an explicit lease, pause or coordinate the owning executor, display authority and expiry, and return control through reconciliation without lost input, duplicated effects, or hidden continued automation.
6. A concurrency journey SHALL prove parent and specialist activity, simultaneous tool calls, agent switching, historical inspection, stale steering rejection, approval routing, cancellation propagation, takeover lease recovery, child failure, parent restart, and criterion-bound synthesis.

## Requirement 58: Security, privacy, performance, and attribution boundaries for the Ion Computer

**User Story:** As a user, I want the computer view to remain safe and honest while displaying external content and sensitive work, so that visibility does not create a new exfiltration, injection, or authority path.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. ALL tool-response content SHALL be treated as untrusted data. Rendering SHALL use inert components with safe URL and media policies, origin isolation where applicable, no script execution, no raw event-handler or stylesheet injection, and no instructions from displayed content entering policy or authority.
2. COMPUTER events, display models, replay, screenshots, caches, exports, and share links SHALL enforce actor, session, project, workspace, agent, and artifact scope using server-side authorization on every fetch rather than client-side hiding.
3. SECRET values, credentials, cookies, tokens, private form fields, sensitive mailbox material, protected file content, and policy-redacted output SHALL be removed before client delivery; the visual event stream SHALL carry write-only references or redacted facts only.
4. APPROVAL and consequence surfaces SHALL identify the real pending operation, target, data movement, external effect, and scope; the visualization SHALL NOT make an unexecuted proposal appear completed or bypass the shared policy manager.
5. THE service SHALL publish and enforce event, delta, payload, retained-history, screenshot, memory, CPU, render-latency, reconnect, and slow-client budgets with bounded coalescing, truncation markers, snapshot fallback, and lossless preservation of terminal status and evidence references.
6. EXTERNAL material SHALL retain source name, URL or provider identity, capture time, revision when available, and observed, generated, summarized, or inferred classification; Ion-native presentation SHALL NOT imply that it is the original external interface.
7. An adversarial suite SHALL prove prompt-injection containment, malicious markup and media rejection, terminal escape neutralization, secret and cross-scope non-disclosure, stale authorization denial, event-flood backpressure, forged event rejection, safe screenshots, and accurate attribution.

## Requirement 59: Ion Computer production acceptance and anti-theater gate

**User Story:** As a user, I want proof that the computer reflects real agent work across tools and restarts, so that the experience is useful operational visibility rather than a polished animation disconnected from execution.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A production GitHub-repository analysis journey SHALL begin from one user request and visibly progress through real search, browsing, repository navigation, code inspection, bounded command or analysis execution, parallel-agent activity when selected, artifact creation, and final report review using actual tool calls and responses.
2. EVERY visible application transition, item, status, error, artifact, and completion claim in the journey SHALL correlate to durable production events and evidence; fixtures, manually injected frontend payloads, disconnected mocks, screenshot-only proof, HTTP success, or SPA fallback SHALL NOT satisfy acceptance.
3. THE journey SHALL survive browser refresh, route change, network interruption, client reconnect, daemon restart, retained-history snapshot fallback, duplicated delivery, parallel out-of-order completion, agent failure, user inspection of history, and Back to live with exact current state.
4. ACCEPTANCE SHALL cover real search and reader pages, GitHub or GitLab, local workspace and Git state, terminal and process output, documents and tabular artifacts, approvals, denial, incomplete and uncertain outcomes, unsupported tools, screenshot fallback, mobile, keyboard, screen reader, and reduced motion.
5. PUBLISHED reference-hardware results SHALL prove bounded event-to-projection latency, animation and scroll responsiveness, reconnect and replay time, browser memory, server memory, payload volume, long-run stability, event-flood behavior, and no tool-execution slowdown caused by disconnected or slow viewers.
6. NO Phase 14 task or umbrella SHALL be marked done until current production binaries and real clients prove criterion-linked artifacts, restart recovery, security and accessibility boundaries, truthful degraded behavior, and zero visual activity without a corresponding authoritative event.
7. THE Ion Computer SHALL remain a contextual projection of the same field-general Ion identity, memory, relationship, policy, goals, approvals, and execution continuity across research, software, data, documents, communications, and future domains; it SHALL NOT create a separate computer-agent identity or restrict the product to software work.

## Requirement 60: Agent-scoped durable scheduling and wake-up

**User Story:** As a user, I want each Ion identity to schedule future and recurring work in its own encrypted scope, so that reminders and autonomous continuation survive restarts without depending on one central scheduler.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE scheduler SHALL support one-time delay, absolute RFC3339 time, standard five-field cron, descriptors, recurring intervals, and IANA time zones with bounded validated inputs and exact next-fire projections.
2. EVERY alarm SHALL be scoped to an authenticated actor and owning session, stored encrypted with its wake message and payload, isolated from every other actor, and deduplicated by an owner-scoped idempotency key.
3. DUE alarms SHALL be durably claimed before delivery and SHALL inject a normal production turn through the authenticated control plane using an occurrence-stable idempotency key so restart or retry cannot create duplicate turns.
4. FAILED delivery SHALL use bounded exponential retry, retain a safe error and attempt count, terminally fail exhausted one-time alarms, and skip-and-advance recurring alarms without wedging the series.
5. THE agent SHALL receive direct create, list, inspect, and cancel schedule tools through the shared tool manager; consequential wake execution SHALL retain normal policy, approval, memory, tool, event, and evidence boundaries.
6. THE operator projection SHALL show owner-safe label, kind, status, next fire, last fire, failures, and last safe error, and SHALL distinguish the existing internal presence schedules from user or agent-created alarms.
7. A production-path suite SHALL prove time zones, once and cron calculation, actor isolation, idempotent creation, due claim, exact-once wake turn, cancellation, bounded retry, recurring skip-and-advance, daemon restart recovery, encrypted-at-rest content, and honest unavailable or degraded state.

## Requirement 61: Versioned Private Computer execution-host contract

**User Story:** As Ion's execution runtime, I want one policy-bound contract for private graphical computers, so that Personal and Clean Linux sessions remain part of the same identity, task, tool, and evidence system across local and hosted infrastructure.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE Private Computer boundary SHALL define versioned host, session, capability, lifecycle-operation, lifecycle-state, authority, resource-budget, persistence, and compatibility contracts without creating a second agent, task, policy, audit, artifact, or completion truth.
2. EVERY privileged host request SHALL bind installation, actor, Ion session, task or outcome, agent, computer session, operation, resource, authority revision, expiry, idempotency key, and replay protection and SHALL fail closed on missing, stale, cross-scope, expired, unsupported, or contradictory values.
3. THE host contract SHALL support provision, start, stop, suspend, resume, rebuild, destroy, inspect, and reconcile plus browser, terminal, filesystem, screenshot, pointer, keyboard, clipboard, desktop-stream, protected-secret-entry, and approved-application capabilities with explicit unavailable and degraded reasons.
4. ION SHALL select execution in the order native structured API or tool, Tavily structured search with bounded SearXNG fallback, semantic fetch or reader extraction, native Chromium/CDP, then graphical computer interaction only when earlier layers are insufficient, direct interaction is required, or the operator explicitly enters the computer.
5. EVERY host transition and computer action SHALL correlate to canonical ComputerEvents, authoritative ToolEvents, policy decisions, leases, artifacts, and evidence records; desktop video and screenshots SHALL remain views and SHALL NOT prove execution or completion.
6. HOST negotiation and reconciliation SHALL preserve explicit stopped, unavailable, provisioning, ready, active, needs-help, disconnected, recovering, failed, and destroyed states across control-plane and host restart, including version incompatibility and orphan detection.
7. A contract suite SHALL prove strict validation, capability negotiation, lifecycle transition legality, idempotent replay, stale-revision rejection, cross-actor and cross-mode isolation, bounded serialization, restart reconciliation, and absence of a second completion truth.

## Requirement 62: Actor-scoped Personal and disposable Clean Computer modes

**User Story:** As an operator, I want a persistent private computer and a clean disposable computer, so that trusted ongoing work can retain explicitly permitted state while risky work starts without prior cookies, files, or account state.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A Personal Computer SHALL use an actor-and-installation-scoped home and workspace volume, retain only explicitly installed applications and approved preferences, and never be mounted or addressable by another actor.
2. A Clean Computer SHALL begin from a version-pinned image and fresh cryptographic and filesystem scope with no Personal cookies, credentials, files, clipboard, account state, package changes, or cache mounted or copied into it.
3. CLEAN completion SHALL export verified produced artifacts through Ion's authoritative artifact path before destroy or cryptographic abandonment and SHALL record cleanup evidence; missing export or cleanup evidence SHALL leave the task incomplete or outcome-unknown.
4. PERSONAL storage controls SHALL include inspect, usage, backup, restore, rebuild, revoke, and clear operations, each policy-routed with explicit consequence, while Clean mode SHALL expose its destruction deadline and retained artifact receipts.
5. RECONCILIATION SHALL detect stopped, unavailable, recovering, orphaned, expired, partially destroyed, and ready environments without reusing stale authority or duplicating actions after either service restarts.
6. CPU, memory, process, storage, network-egress, idle-time, session-duration, screenshot, clipboard, and cost budgets SHALL be declared per mode and enforced independently of provider token budgets.
7. A real-host suite SHALL prove Personal restart retention, Clean freshness and destruction, artifact-before-cleanup gating, orphan recovery, storage exhaustion behavior, budget enforcement, and no cross-actor or cross-mode state leakage.

## Requirement 63: Live private desktop view and coordinated operator takeover

**User Story:** As an operator, I want to watch and temporarily control Ion's real desktop inside the existing Ion Computer, so that I can resolve graphical boundaries without hidden automation, secret leakage, or a separate remote-desktop product.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE existing Ion Computer shell SHALL render a real private_desktop application from an authenticated desktop stream isolated from the trusted operator DOM while preserving the persistent conversation, evidence rail, timeline, Follow live, history, full-screen, responsive, and accessibility behaviors.

5. THE view SHALL show Personal or Clean mode and Ion has control, You have control, or Control reconciling plus honest provisioning, ready, active, needs-help, disconnected, recovering, stopped, failed, and unavailable states without fabricated cursor, typing, progress, or completion.
6. PROTECTED secret entry SHALL suspend or redact screenshots, clipboard capture, event content, logs, and model-visible observations while recording only a bounded redacted fact and SHALL require explicit exit before automation resumes.
7. STREAM transport SHALL be bounded, reconnectable, and replaceable without changing semantic truth; public Railway WebSocket sessions SHALL reconnect before the platform request-duration ceiling and SHALL recover from duplicate frames, route changes, control-plane restart, and computer-service restart.
8. A real-client journey SHALL prove authenticated viewing, mobile and keyboard use, needs-help takeover, one operator interaction, lease renewal and expiry, no concurrent executor input, protected secret entry, return-control reconciliation, reconnect, restart, and semantic-event continuity.

## Requirement 64: Railway one-click single-service appliance deployment

**User Story:** As a new operator, I want to deploy the complete Ion appliance as one Railway service, so that Ion, its private computer, and Office Studio reach a truthful ready or unavailable state without extra service setup or Railway-only data formats.

THE appliance SHALL expose one aggregate liveness and readiness endpoint while retaining distinct Ion, ion-computer, ONLYOFFICE, compatibility, migration, and usable-desktop state internally; the Railway health check SHALL gate public activation while continuous supervision and reconciliation detect later child failure.

PUBLIC streaming SHALL support Railway HTTP/1.1 WebSockets with bounded frames, exponential-backoff reconnect before the current request-duration ceiling, replay cursors, and origin checks; ion-computer and ONLYOFFICE traffic SHALL use authenticated loopback endpoints and SHALL never bind a public control port.

RESTART, rollback, child-process failure, and image incompatibility SHALL preserve authoritative encrypted state, prevent two writers from sharing the one volume, reconcile in-flight sessions, document saves, and leases, and surface unavailable rather than silently starting an incompatible or unauthenticated component.

8. THE deployment SHALL support documented export and migration to ordinary container infrastructure without Railway-only state formats, privileged mode, a public control port, or an unauthenticated fallback.

ADVERSARIAL tests SHALL cover hostile pages and downloads, malicious clipboard and terminal content, cross-actor and cross-mode access, stale and replayed tickets, lost leases, reconnect storms, orphaned processes, resource exhaustion, storage failure, partial cleanup, incompatible versions, and control-plane and host restart.

A production deployment journey SHALL prove SearXNG-first research, semantic or Chromium escalation, a real graphical boundary, authenticated live desktop, needs-help takeover, operator interaction, duplicate-safe resume, artifact creation and verification, service restarts, Personal retention, and Clean destruction after artifact export.

NO Private Computer task or umbrella SHALL be marked done from code presence, simulated payloads, screenshots, HTTP 200, video, or model claims; current production binaries and clients SHALL provide criterion-linked authoritative evidence, and unresolved platform capability or deployment boundaries SHALL remain visible.

## Requirement 66: Secure durable image and video generation studio

**User Story:** As an operator, I want a first-class media studio inside Ion, so that I can generate and edit images and videos through domain-specific providers without exposing credentials or losing work when a browser or daemon restarts.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE mounted Media Studio SHALL provide text-to-image, image-to-image, text-to-video, image-to-video, inpainting, cleanup, background removal and replacement, text removal, face merge, and upscaling workflows with mode-specific validated controls, accessible previews, honest status, history, and downloads.
2. PROVIDER credentials SHALL remain server-side and SHALL enter neither browser bundles, control-plane payloads, logs, diagnostics, model context, nor persisted job metadata; browser mutations SHALL require the authenticated actor, exact origin, and CSRF proof.
3. PROMPTS, negative prompts, uploaded source images, masks, and face references SHALL be encrypted at rest; jobs, provider task IDs, progress, safe failures, and locally owned output assets SHALL survive browser refresh and daemon restart with actor isolation on every list, inspect, asset, and delete request.
4. ASYNC provider execution SHALL durably record submission before polling, reconcile in-flight provider task IDs after restart, bound time, retries, payloads, output count, and output bytes, and report failure or unknown outcome honestly without duplicate paid generation.
5. REMOTE provider and output retrieval SHALL require TLS, block private and special-use destinations across redirects and DNS resolution, bound response bodies, verify supported image or video media types, and copy expiring provider outputs into Ion-owned storage before success is projected.
6. THE initial provider adapter SHALL implement the Novita V3 contracts supplied in temp/novita_api_examples while keeping provider base URL, client, models, and workflow mapping replaceable for future domain-specific media adapters.
7. A production-path suite SHALL prove authentication, CSRF, actor isolation, encrypted inputs, validation, synchronous edit output, asynchronous generation and polling, restart recovery, provider rejection and timeout, SSRF denial, output bounds, durable playback and download, responsive accessibility, and honest unconfigured state.

## Requirement 67: Deployment username and password authentication

**User Story:** As the owner of a deployed Ion instance, I want to configure its operator username and password through deployment variables, so that the dashboard and every operator API remain private on Railway and ordinary container hosts.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. ION SHALL accept exactly one deployment username plus either a deployment password or an Argon2id PHC password hash, validate complete configuration at startup, keep credential material server-side, and never expose it through browser assets, API responses, logs, diagnostics, model context, or durable state.
2. PASSWORD verification SHALL use Argon2id with a unique random salt for plaintext deployment input, constant-time comparison, bounded input sizes, a generic rejection response, and a bounded login-attempt limiter that does not reveal whether the username or password was wrong.
3. THE browser SHALL provide an accessible first-party login experience plus authenticated status and logout, and successful login SHALL issue short-lived signed Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Strict session cookies with a separately bound CSRF token while logout SHALL invalidate both cookies.
4. LOGIN SHALL require an exact configured origin, JSON content type, bounded request body, and safe method handling; every authenticated mutation SHALL continue to require actor authentication, exact origin, and CSRF proof.
5. WHEN deployment authentication is configured, unauthenticated document requests SHALL receive no actor identity or session credential, operator APIs SHALL reject access, and authenticated document requests SHALL receive the actor bootstrap without embedding any credential.
6. ION SHALL fail closed when authentication configuration is partial, ambiguous, or disabled on a non-loopback origin or detected Railway deployment; loopback-only development MAY retain the existing automatic local operator session.
7. A production-path suite SHALL prove valid login, invalid and throttled login, status, logout, expiry, restart invalidation, cookie properties, CSRF, origin, payload bounds, no credential leakage, unauthenticated API denial, authenticated browser use, and Railway fail-closed configuration.

## Requirement 68: Encrypted agent-native Office Studio with ONLYOFFICE editing

**User Story:** As a user, I want a first-class document, spreadsheet, presentation, and PDF studio inside Ion, so that I can create, edit, version, and manage office documents with the same identity, encryption, and agent capabilities as every other Ion workflow.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE mounted Office Studio SHALL provide real document, spreadsheet, presentation, PDF/form, template, upload, library, editor, version, restore, archive, download and export workflows with accessible responsive states.
2. ION is the canonical actor-scoped document manager and storage service; every committed version is encrypted at rest, content-hashed, immutable, bounded and durable across browser and daemon restart.
3. A replaceable OfficeEngine contract separates Ion from ONLYOFFICE-specific editor configuration, health, force-save, disconnect, conversion and compatibility behavior.
4. Browser operations require the authenticated Ion actor, exact origin and CSRF for mutations; engine configurations, callbacks, downloads and commands use short-lived scoped tokens and validated JWTs without exposing shared secrets.
5. Save callbacks are bounded, authenticated, idempotent and restart-safe; Ion validates and durably commits a downloaded version before acknowledging success, and duplicate, stale, uncertain or failed saves remain honest.
6. Imports and exports validate supported extensions, MIME signatures, OOXML archive structure, decompression bounds, macros, embedded content and maximum sizes; macro-enabled or dangerous documents are quarantined or opened read-only.
7. Agent office operations preserve the same Ion identity, memory, task, approval, evidence and artifact boundaries; selected content is sent only by explicit user action and proposed document mutations remain reviewable.
8. THE editor is mounted through a same-origin WebSocket-capable proxy or another explicitly configured secure origin; direct unauthenticated document-server exposure and arbitrary proxy targets are prohibited.
9. COMPOSE, Kubernetes and Helm packaging use a pinned configurable ONLYOFFICE image, while Railway packages that pinned engine inside the single Ion appliance service; every target uses sealed JWT authentication, non-public engine access, health checks, durable canonical Ion versions, graceful save/disconnect behavior and documented resource requirements.
10. COMMUNITY branding, AGPL obligations, connection limits and unavailable commercial features remain visible; the domain must support later Developer or hosted engines without data migration.
11. PRODUCTION acceptance covers real DOCX, XLSX, PPTX and PDF journeys, JWT/origin/CSRF denial, cross-actor isolation, callback replay, restart, WebSocket reconnect, malicious files, version restore, backup, export and artifact verification.
12. NO Office task is marked complete from source presence, an iframe rendering, HTTP 200, simulated callbacks, screenshots or model claims.
